subject: Transect design theory VS fieldwork data collection challenges

messages.author: d2ed14049df3de48
messages.subject: Transect design theory VS fieldwork data collection challenges
parts:
Dear all,
Apologies if this issue has already been covered.
I have designed transects for marine mammal surveys which are currently taking place.
I have started receiving tracks of the vessel and some are far from fitting to the designed transects (see below).
Obviously there is always a difference between what we design on our computer and what we can achieve at sea. But my question is: to what extend does that have an impact on the analysis that will take place afterwards. In this example, how badly would that be likely to impact my results?
Thank you very much.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] Transect design theory VS fieldwork data collection challenges
parts:
Jérôme

It is good to examine results as they are coming from your ongoing survey.  As you note, departures from designed survey tracks do occur. The deviations you show do no make me overly concerned about your results.  Remember at the time of analysis to use realised survey effort in the calculations, not the theoretical effort.
